title: REPORT on the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Facility
part_text: 18. Notes that only 13 Member States have requested loans and that EUR 92 billion of the EUR 385.8 billion available will remain unused since this amount was not committed by the deadline of 31 December 2023; takes note of the fact that loans were only attractive for Member States that faced higher borrowing costs on the financial markets or that sought to compensate for a reduction in RRF grants; points out that some Member States have made limited use of RRF loans, either due to strong fiscal positions or administrative considerations; calls on the Commission to consider, in this regard, the risks and inefficiencies of joint borrowing before proposing any EU financial instruments in the future; considers that a political discussion is mandatory on the use of unspent funds in the light of tight public budgets, the amounts at stake and urgent EU strategic priorities; calls for an assessment of how and under which conditions unused RRF funds could be redirected to boost Europe’s competitiveness, resilience, the European defence industry, and social, economic and territorial cohesion;
